Independent planar cap moment calculations (five radii)
correctness.rationale: Radial covariance gives E[y_i y_j]=q_d delta_ij, making the reproducing kernel exactly K(x,y)=1+x dot y/q_d. Symmetry and radial convexity of integral |K| put the sharp output at outer |x|=1; sign of K gives extremizing input and symmetric kernel gives matching L1 norm. Kernel has unit signed mass, so endpoint norm is one plus twice the negative cap moment, outer ball minus inner ball, with correct volume normalization. A uniform-shell radius coupling proves 0<=q_d’(r)<=r/d<1, so r-q_d(r) has exactly one zero in (1/(d+2),1/d). At inner-ball contact, h=r-q_d(r)>0 small and the cap beta integral has order h^((d+3)/2) with coefficient 4 omega_{d-1} 2^((d-1)/2) r_d^((d-3)/2)/((d+1)(d+3)). Multiplication by 2/(omega_d(1-r_d^d)) and h’=1-q_d’ yields claimed C_d>0. This term is one-sided, so its derivative order is ceil((d+3)/2). Planar q2=(1+r²)/4 yields r2=2-sqrt3; independently checked numerical cap moments and elementary circular formula at five radii. Computations do not substitute for all-d proof.

Prior polynomial projection stability studies on filled disk and balls
value.rationale: Sharp endpoint stability under a concentric drilled hole is a natural geometric perturbation of an elementary polynomial projection. A unique contact point changes exactly which kernel-negative cap is removed, producing a dimension-universal first nonsmooth derivative and explicit threshold, a meaningful shape-sensitivity invariant.
residual_risks: Restricted to affine projection and concentric uniform Euclidean shells.

final_claim: For uniform Euclidean shells A_{d,r} with integer d>=2 and 0<=r<1, affine L2-orthogonal projection has sharp L1/L∞ norm 1+2(F_d(1,q_d(r))-F_d(r,q_d(r)))/(omega_d(1-r^d)), with q_d=(1-r^(d+2))/((d+2)(1-r^d)); unique contact r_d=q_d(r_d), cusp exponent (d+3)/2 with explicit positive coefficient; planar contact 2-sqrt(3).
